key_insight: Strong guideline recall did not translate into patient-specific evidence use across ten medical LLMs.
clinical_relevance: Medical LLM evaluation should test evidence application in clinical scenarios, not just guideline knowledge.
method: Built Med Evidence Bench with 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels.
Linked each medical-claim scoring criterion to a versioned source-text span.
Evaluated ten LLMs and compared automated grading with physician judgments.
evidence_signal: Evidence Trace Scores ranged from 0.975–0.997 for guideline knowledge versus 0.182–0.447 for real-world scenarios; automated grading achieved macro-F1 0.930 against physician-majority judgments.
watch_item: Results from Chinese-language materials do not establish clinical effectiveness, and grading agreement was lower for evidence application.
paper_title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
